filed_edges: [ANSWERED 2026-08-12 BY MEASUREMENT] WHAT IS THE FIRST WRITER? The edge's own candidate is REFUTED. The ground-loop liveness record does NOT collapse two builds into one: it already reaches disk — pid 109150 was running `python3 -m cairn.devices.ground_loop` and ~/.cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/0/liveness.json carried a current, advancing stamp — and it closes NEITHER of the two findings this ticket exists to close. Finding #4 is that set_diagnostic_receiver has no live caller (re-measured today: 1 definition, 1 passthrough, zero live call sites); finding #5 is that no device-emitted record exists on disk. liveness.json is an OVERWRITTEN SNAPSHOT of device state, and neither finding is about device state. THE FIRST WRITER IS THE SAME PROCESS BY A DIFFERENT PATH: the resident ground loop, through its own emit() gate contacts (9 of them in loop.py; 'subscribe' fires during startup, so the falsifier's 'do nothing else' has a record to find), once a disk-backed receiver is wired at cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/__main__.py — the one place that hands the resident device the real world. So the ticket IS buildable, and it is one build, not two.

[DISTINCTION RECORDED, NOT A SILENT CONTRADICTION] WHERE THE LOG LANDS. The trouble's finding #5 names ~/.cairn/logs/ as the empty place, and that is where it looked. Akien ruled the address question on 2026-08-12, after the trouble was written, and his test is OWNERSHIP rather than depth: 'a file that answers "what is true of this machine" lives at the top; a file that answers "what is true of this device" lives under devices/<name>/<instance>/' — with logs, backups and venv named as legitimately top-level machine-scoped things (recorded verbatim in cairn/tools/base/address.py). A device's breadcrumb trail is that device's state, so it lands at instance/devices/<device>/<instance>/diagnostics.jsonl, resolved through cairn.tools.base.address.instance_path and never hand-spelled. Finding #5's measurement stands; its address is superseded by the newer ruling.
closed_by: THE FALSIFIER RUN VERBATIM, not a proof calling in. Stopped the resident loop (SIGTERM, clean), relaunched it from the launcher's own line, did nothing else, and read from a separate shell: 13 records at ~/.cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/0/diagnostics.jsonl and 18 at ~/.cairn/devices/bus/0/diagnostics.jsonl, every one home='sent' — the first 'sent' in the system's history, stamped in the same second the pid liveness.json names was born. WHAT WAS BUILT: cairn/machines/diagnostic_inspector/log.py (BreadcrumbLog — a pure-append JSONL receiver answering the same two contracts the in-memory Mailbox answers, addressed through cairn.tools.base.address.instance_path), wired in two lines at cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/__main__.py for BOTH live devices. Sealed under the tester in netns; 10 teeth, 39 assertions; nine chart criteria run by their instruments and twelve hypotheses confirmed (verdict-20260812T160242-aaf1d681e970). THE DISTINCTIONS WORTH CARRYING. (1) The filed edge was REFUTED by measurement rather than answered: liveness.json already reached disk and closes neither finding, because it is an overwritten SNAPSHOT of device state and the findings are about a TRAIL. The two files now sit in the same directory and the adjacency is the distinction on display. (2) The ADDRESS MOVED under the ticket: finding #5 named ~/.cairn/logs/, and Akien's later ownership ruling (2026-08-12, recorded in cairn/tools/base/address.py) sends a device's own state under devices/<name>/<instance>/ — recorded on the trouble rather than silently contradicted. (3) BOTH devices wired, not one — closing the loop and leaving the BusDevice held would have closed half the finding in the same three lines. (4) The trail is QUIET AT REST: beats 58 -> 71 while both files held their line counts, so it is a breadcrumb trail and not a firehose. (5) The clearance gate asked for two things on the way — this ticket had no owning_intention and cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop's charter declared no gated_by — both filled at the crossing that needed them, which is the field's stated policy rather than a backfill. WHAT THE FIRST UNATTENDED OUTPUT ALREADY SAYS, and nobody asked it to: the bus trail's 17 'undelivered' records name their own lack — 'harbor_master was discovered by its probes/ folder, not registered with a device — it is on the roster to be PULSED, not to be paged' — which is the standing probescan trouble (19 probes BROKEN, one fault wearing nineteen faces) diagnosing itself on disk.
